metadata.description: Open agent skills by Ian Balina: playbooks AI agents can run end to end, starting with fundraising.

plugins.name: fundraising
plugins.description: Run a raise, or the sale of a company, from start to finish: a startup seed or venture round, a fund raise from LPs, or a company sale. All of them run as one process, and a person approves before anything goes out.

plugins.name: first-principles-thinking
plugins.description: Reason from first principles instead of copying what came before. Take a decision, a design, a cost, or a plan down to the claims that have real evidence. Price the raw inputs where money is involved. Then build a better option up from the floor.

plugins.name: game-theory-for-decisions
plugins.description: Decide when the result depends on what other people do. Map who is playing, what each one gains or loses, who knows what, and who moves when. Work out how they are likely to answer. Then choose the best move, or change the game. For negotiations, competition, enforcement, auctions, and cooperation.

plugins.name: comms
plugins.description: Founder communications as a set of steps: name the moment, decide who speaks, work out how the audience already sees you, build the story, say it plainly and say it yourself, and keep your answers disciplined after it lands. For announcements, launches, crises, and everyday content.

plugins.name: write-in-your-voice
plugins.description: Build a working voice for a person from how they actually speak, then draft in it. Build a bank of their own words from their speech, kept in a fixed order, most trusted first. Draft from their own sentences. Check the words, and check the shape of the draft too. And keep a record of which drafts the person kills.

plugins.name: fix-the-bottleneck
plugins.description: A Theory of Constraints procedure for running systems. State the goal as throughput. Measure every stage. Find the one constraint. Get more from it, and set everything else to its pace, before you spend to lift it. Then measure again, and keep going until the output moves.

plugins.name: stop-the-scroll
plugins.description: A procedure for building content: AIDA, with the ends hardened. The hook and the call to action are each built to stand out among a hundred pieces, and to stand alone with nothing around them, over a middle anyone can follow, about impact.

plugins.name: cold-outreach
plugins.description: How to write cold email and cold DMs that earn replies, built from evidence that was checked, not advice nobody ever tested. Test the offer. Build the batch from a trigger. Check the warm path and the history. Research one true observation. Ask one question about interest.

plugins.name: positioning
plugins.description: Decide what a product will be thought of as, on buyer evidence, in a fixed order: what buyers would do instead, what the product uniquely has, what that is worth with proof, who cares most, and the category last. No position ships without named trade-offs. Returns a positioning record a marketing plan can consume directly.

plugins.name: one-page-marketing-plan
plugins.description: Build the whole marketing system on one page: diagnosis first, then nine squares - target, message, media, capture, nurture, convert, experience, lifetime value, referrals - each standing on measured evidence about how buyers behave, with the brand-versus-activation split stated as a hypothesis with a review date.

plugins.name: interview-yourself
plugins.description: An AI interviewer that asks questions a stranger already cares about, with the receipt from your own week and the numbers attached, so your answers out loud become posts.

plugins.name: business-model-canvas
plugins.description: State how a business makes money on one sheet, and test it. A fit test picks the Lean Canvas while the model is still being searched for, or the nine-block Business Model Canvas once it is found. Fill it from evidence, then rank the riskiest assumptions, each with its next test.

plugins.name: vision-and-manifesto
plugins.description: Write a vision, mission, or manifesto that does work. One core set of beliefs at three lengths: the vision as a picturable future with a number on it, the mission as the work now, and a manifesto only when a public job exists for one. It ships only when the statements change real decisions about hiring, firing, and money.

plugins.name: inbound-sponsorship
plugins.description: Run the inbound sponsorship desk for a media property: triage inquiries against a bar, sort them into pricing lanes, negotiate on evidence, structure hybrid deals with a floor, and run each placement through its lifecycle to renewal.

plugins.name: podcast-yourself
plugins.description: Prep a talking-head video before the camera rolls. Mine the performer's own posts for the shapes that already worked, sort every claim by who can say it, and build a riff sheet — one question per beat, the receipt to hit, the line to land — plus the edit brief the footage is cut under.

plugins.name: storytelling
plugins.description: Design a story that holds to the end: the arc, the structure, the hook, the scenes, the ending. Every lesson carries its evidence label — measured, practitioner, framing, platform-declared, or observed — and the skill hands off scene cards a producer can build from.

plugins.name: cartoon-system
plugins.description: Keep a recurring character recognisably the same across every image. A character bible holds the cast, each image is generated against the approved images before it, and a drift check fails anything that wanders before it ships. Images only; text layers are optional and off by default.

plugins.name: funnel-operator
plugins.description: Run a video channel as a system, not as one-off uploads. The channel is set up once as a single config file, and every episode moves through the same nine stages, with distribution to the channel's other platforms and a scoreboard reading the funnel end to end.

plugins.name: playbook
plugins.description: The router for the Made Man Playbooks. Hand it a task with no skills named: it classifies the task, selects the skills whose triggers match, runs each for real and in order — understand, decide, position, plan, say — and merges the results into one deliverable.
